title: Building a drinks shelf
target: How to set out the drinks a Supermarket Simulator shop carries, given that soda, water, juice, beer and wine are separate named goods with containers of their own.
prerequisites: Shelf space for a drinks row

steps.do: Order soda by brand rather than as one line of cola.
steps.because: the game names six sodas, each with a model of its own (SM_Soda_Cola, SM_Soda_Zap, SM_Soda_Kouje, SM_Soda_Pulp, SM_Soda_Ropico, SM_Soda_Turko)

steps.do: Give the bottled water a row of its own.
steps.because: three bottled waters are named for the brands they carry (SM_Bottled Water_Aotte, SM_Bottled Water_Fort-lacs, SM_Bottled Water_Montcuq)

steps.do: Put the juice out in the shape the game ships it.
steps.because: the juice brand is carried on the pack and on the model that stands in the shop (SM_Orange Juice_Bio Juice, Orange Juice_Bio Juice)

steps.do: Keep the beer apart from the rest of the drinks.
steps.because: beer arrives as a bottle, a keg and a pack, and there is a beer house with a collider of its own (M_Beer, M_Beerkeg, M_Beerpack, SM_BeerHouse_Collider)

steps.do: Stand the wine so its label faces the aisle.
steps.because: the wine bottle and its printed labels are art the game ships (M_Wine, Wine Chebon, Wine_Pouilleux)

steps.do: Match the shelf shape to the container instead of forcing one shelf to hold everything.
steps.because: the containers are modelled apart from the goods themselves (M_SodaCan, M_Cans_A, M_Juice_A, M_WaterPack)

commonMistakes: Treating every soda as one product and leaving five brands unordered.
Putting bottled water and juice on the same line because the bottles look alike.
Storing the keg where a shelf slot should be and blocking the aisle.
Buying wine before checking it has a label side to face out.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
